newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police release suspect in arson case.
newsitem.headline: German police release suspect in arson case.

text.p: German police said on Monday they had freed a man held in connection with an arson attack on church property in which assailants also spray-painted swastikas on a wall.

Police in the northern city of Luebeck said the 33-year-old was released because there was no firm evidence linking him with Sunday's attack on a kindergarten in a Christian community centre which also includes a church.
No one was injured but the attackers daubed a slogan on a wall threatening Guenter Harig, a Protestant churchman and campaigner for the rights of asylum-seekers.

Harig vowed on Monday he would not be intimated by the threats and would continue to support families seeking asylum. His name was also found daubed at the scene of another attack in Luebeck last month, which destroyed a Roman Catholic church.
A 19-year-old man has been detained on suspicion of starting that blaze, one of a string of attacks on churches in northern Germany over the past few weeks.

Last week, vandals spray-painted swastikas on the Luebeck office of Germany's best known author, Guenter Grass, and on another local church. The left-leaning novelist had publicly backed Harig's social campaigning.
